clue.text: Board whose sittings are said to be nightly

definitions.text: Board whose sittings are said to be nightly

parts.words: Board whose sittings are said to be nightly
parts.note: the board is a piece of furniture where Arthur's men sat, and 'nightly' sounds like 'knightly'

explanation.surface: A committee is said to hold its meetings every night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee, but it is the famous table of Camelot; 'nightly' is said like 'knightly', since knights sat at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's knights met at a circular piece of furniture, so it was a board where knights sat.

clue.text: Cyril Connolly-type pool significant to Eustace and Hilda

definitions.meaning: Connolly's novel is The ... Pool, so his kind of pool is a stony one
in L. P. Hartley's Eustace and Hilda trilogy the children play at a seaside pool among the stones of the shore

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are literary: Connolly's only novel is The Rock Pool, and L. P. Hartley's The Shrimp and the Anemone opens with Eustace and Hilda at a pool among stones on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Connolly's novel title names this kind of seaside pool, and the stony shore pool is where Hartley's children begin their story.

clue.text: Essential elements of Hydriotophia

parts.note: Sir Thomas Browne's Hydriotaphia is subtitled Urn Burial, so its essential objects are funerary vessels

explanation.surface: A chemist lists the basic components of some obscure substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' suggests chemistry, but Hydriotaphia, or Urn Burial (1658), is Browne's meditation on ancient burial vessels dug up in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Browne's treatise is about burial vessels unearthed in Norfolk, so those vessels are its essential subject.

clue.text: A verra weel kent man in this part of Scotland

definitions.text: A verra weel kent man in this part of Scotland

parts.words: A verra weel kent man in this part of Scotland
parts.note: 'verra weel kent' is Scots for 'very well known'; the man is the doctor of Tannochbrae in A. J. Cronin's stories

explanation.surface: A local in Scots dialect speaks of a very well-known figure of the district.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Cronin's Scottish country doctor, of the fictional town of Tannochbrae, became a famous BBC television series; the Scots spelling sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronin's fictional general practitioner was the best-known figure of his Scottish small town.

clue.text: Astringent expert gets British backing

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for British goes in reverse

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued specialist is supported by the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' means the British abbreviation is reversed before it joins the expert; 'Astringent' is the definition, not a description of the expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is an old synonym of acerbic: sour, harsh, sharp to the taste.

clue.text: Money gets suit back for Tennyson's poet-hero

parts.note: lucre is money, especially ill-gotten

indicators.note: back means the word suit is written in reverse after the money

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cash buys a returned suit for the hero of a Victorian poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUIT into TIUS. Tennyson's dramatic monologue Lucretius is spoken by the Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson wrote a monologue about the Roman author of De Rerum Natura, making that poet its hero.

clue.text: A hard sailor man for Jezebel

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A tough seaman is just the man for a scheming woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' here means husband: in the Bible King Ahab of Israel was Jezebel's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Kings the Israelite king who married Jezebel was her husband.

clue.text: Brain, say, for Forester protagonist

definitions.meaning: Dennis Brain was a celebrated English player of the French horn
C. S. Forester's naval novels follow Horatio, a Royal Navy officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brain' is not the organ but Dennis Brain, the famous horn player; 'Forester' is not a woodsman but the novelist C. S. Forester.
explanation.definitionFit: A horn player is one who blows a horn, as Dennis Brain did; Forester's naval hero bears that surname.

clue.text: Sprint by Arnold hero is nonsense

indicators.note: by means beside, so the sprint sits next to the hero

parts.note: Matthew Arnold's poem Balder Dead has the Norse god as its hero
a dash is a sprint

explanation.surface: A running race next to a poet's hero is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold wrote Balder Dead about the Norse god; 'by' places DASH beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is a synonym of senseless talk or rubbish.

clue.text: That of a king caught in play in Elsinore

definitions.text: That of a king caught in play in Elsinore

parts.words: That of a king caught in play in Elsinore
parts.note: Hamlet says 'the play's the thing / Wherein I'll catch the ... of the king' at Elsinore

explanation.surface: A monarch's something is trapped during a performance at a Danish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet stages The Mousetrap to watch Claudius's guilt: 'the play's the thing wherein I'll catch the conscience of the king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line names the king's inner moral sense as what the play would catch.

clue.text: Examination in Tudor alchemy

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A test on alchemy in sixteenth-century England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into tudOR ALchemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination is called an oral, as in a viva.

clue.text: Ben Rosenblum gets involved in Herricks splendid editions

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled together, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar named Ben Rosenblum works on fine editions of Herrick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved' rearranges BEN ROSENBLUM. Robert Herrick's religious poems were published as His Noble Numbers (1648).
explanation.definitionFit: Herrick's sacred verses were titled with 'noble' meaning splendid and 'numbers' meaning verses.

clue.text: Blueblood due to be thoroughly upset before work and difficulty

indicators.note: being thoroughly upset means these letters are completely jumbled

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is due to be thrown into turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be thoroughly upset' rearranges the first two words. The witches in Macbeth chant 'Double, double toil and trouble', so the phrase comes before work ('toil') and difficulty ('trouble').
explanation.definitionFit: In the witches' chant this repeated word precedes toil and trouble, synonyms of work and difficulty.

clue.text: It is used for writing in French

definitions.text: It is used for writing in French

parts.words: It is used for writing in French
parts.note: read as a piece of furniture for writing, whose name comes from French

explanation.surface: Something is used when writing in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as being about writing in the French language, but it means a writing desk, a word borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived word names a writing desk or bureau.

clue.text: Hastings: "Hath the — — full commission, / In very ample virtue of his father… ?" (King Henry IV, Part II)

definitions.text: Hastings: "Hath the — — full commission, / In very ample virtue of his father… ?" (King Henry IV, Part II)

parts.words: Hastings: "Hath the — — full commission, / In very ample virtue of his father… ?" (King Henry IV, Part II)
parts.note: Hastings asks at Gaultree whether the king's younger son, Lancaster, holds full powers from his father

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's history play with two words left out.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 4 the rebels parley with Henry IV's son John of Lancaster, called by title and name in the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words are the title and forename of Henry IV's son, John of Lancaster.

clue.text: First fag I punished for scratches on tile

indicators.note: punished suggests being knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: At a public school the senior boy's servant is disciplined for marking the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punished' rearranges FIRST FAG I. A fag was a junior boy at a British public school who ran errands for a senior.
explanation.definitionFit: Sgraffito is decoration made by scratching through a surface layer, as on pottery tiles.

clue.text: Illusory as Julian Mitchell's toys

definitions.meaning: illusory means unreal, existing only in the mind
Julian Mitchell's first novel was ... Toys (1961)

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the first word of Julian Mitchell's novel title Imaginary Toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is unreal or fancied, and Mitchell's novel title calls its toys by that adjective.

clue.text: Name dropped by None But The Lonely Heart's author

definitions.text: Name dropped by None But The Lonely Heart's author

parts.words: Name dropped by None But The Lonely Heart's author
parts.note: Richard Llewellyn, author of None But the Lonely Heart, was born with a further surname that he did not write under

explanation.surface: A novelist is accused of name-dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name dropped' sounds like name-dropping, but Richard Llewellyn's full name was Richard Dafydd Vivian Llewellyn Lloyd, and he dropped the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: The author's real surname was left off his pen-name, so it is the surname he dropped.

clue.text: French philologist initiates really English nomenclature at Nantes

indicators.note: initiates suggests the starting letters, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A French scholar of language introduces English naming in Nantes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiates' takes the first letter of really English nomenclature at Nantes. Ernest Renan was a French philologist and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Renan, author of the Life of Jesus, was a nineteenth-century French scholar of Semitic languages.

clue.text: Lord and Lady Clonbrony, for example

definitions.text: Lord and Lady Clonbrony, for example

parts.words: Lord and Lady Clonbrony, for example
parts.note: the Clonbronys are the Irish landlords living in London in Maria Edgeworth's novel The Absentee

explanation.surface: A couple from the Irish peerage are given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Edgeworth's The Absentee (1812) is about Irish landowners who live in England, away from their estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgeworth's Clonbronys are landlords living away from their Irish estates, examples of people not present.

clue.text: Eliot's chilly travellers with cold host in Thomas novel

parts.note: T. S. Eliot's Journey of the Magi begins 'A cold coming we had of it'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a host is an army

explanation.surface: Eliot's wise men on their freezing journey are joined by a crowd in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Leslie Thomas wrote The Magic Army (1981), about wartime Devon; 'host' is the old sense of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Army is a novel by Leslie Thomas.

clue.text: "Wherein of —s vast and desarts idle, Rough quarries, rocks and hills" (Othello)

definitions.text: "Wherein of —s vast and desarts idle, Rough quarries, rocks and hills" (Othello)

parts.words: "Wherein of —s vast and desarts idle, Rough quarries, rocks and hills" (Othello)
parts.note: Othello tells the senate of his travels through great caves, deserts and hills

explanation.surface: A line from Othello with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word is an old poetic word for a cave, from Othello's speech to the senate in Act 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Antre is an archaic word for a cave or cavern, as used by Othello.

clue.text: Sister of Kronos, powerless to fly

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Kronos married his Titan sister, mother of Zeus
a large flightless South American bird cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the South American flightless bird of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titaness mother of Zeus shares her name with a large flightless South American bird.

clue.text: Cheap second edition of Old St Paul's describes church, in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A cheap reprint of Ainsworth's novel Old St Paul's describes the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' picks letters from cheAP SEcond. Old St Paul's is a novel by W. Harrison Ainsworth; 'church' stands for a part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Sacred symbol I study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A believer contemplates a holy image.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image venerated in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Sussex town is trendy in Douglas Reeman work

parts.note: Battle is a town in East Sussex, site of the 1066 battle
's is the short form of is
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable Sussex town appears in a naval novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives S as in 'Battle's hip'. Battle is the East Sussex town by the site of the Battle of Hastings; Douglas Reeman wrote the naval novel Battleship.
explanation.definitionFit: Battleship (1987) is a naval novel by Douglas Reeman.

clue.text: "Eternities glimpsed in one single onslaught" (Meipso)

indicators.note: glimpsed in means the letters are seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Endless time is glimpsed in a single rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glimpsed in' points into singlE ONSlaught.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immeasurably long ages, the same idea as eternities.

clue.text: Spy Rebecca, masquerading in virtual reality

indicators.note: masquerading means disguised, so the letters appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A female spy called Rebecca operates in disguise online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masquerading' rearranges SPY REBECCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional realm of computer networks, a simulated online world.
